sources.entry: Bencher - Suite of continuous benchmarking tools designed to catch performance regressions in CI. (Source Code) MIT/Apache-2.0 Rust

summary.one_liner: Bencher is a continuous benchmarking platform (CLI, API server, and web console) that runs benchmarks locally or in CI and flags performance regressions before they merge.
summary.what_it_does: The bencher CLI runs your existing benchmarks and stores the results on a Bencher server. The web console tracks, queries, and graphs results over time by source branch, testbed, benchmark, and measure. Analytics detect regressions against configurable thresholds and alerts, and the GitHub Action can comment on pull requests with a report. The README lists adapters for many harnesses, including Rust (libtest bench, Criterion, Iai, Gungraun), Go (go test -bench), Python (pytest-benchmark), C++ (Google Benchmark, Catch2), JavaScript (Benchmark.js, Vitest), and generic JSON, plus build-time and file-size tracking. Bencher Bare Metal runners are offered as a hosted option for more consistent results than shared CI runners. The suite is available as Bencher Cloud or self-hosted via Docker, Kubernetes, or bare metal.
use_cases: catch performance regressions in pull requests
track benchmark results over time with graphs
continuous benchmarking in GitHub Actions or GitLab CI
track build time and binary file size
compare benchmark runs on consistent hardware
how_to_run: uses: bencherdev/bencher@main (GitHub Actions step to install the CLI)
Set BENCHER_PROJECT and BENCHER_API_TOKEN environment variables
See the Self-Hosted Quickstart for on-prem deployment
notable: Bare metal runners aim to remove the >30% variance typical of shared CI runners
Supports many benchmark harnesses across Rust, Go, Python, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, Ruby, Dart, and Shell (Hyperfine)
Can fail CI on alerts (--error-on-alert) or comment results on PRs
Available as hosted Bencher Cloud or self-hosted deployment
caveats: Bare metal runners and Bencher Cloud are paid, billed by the minute (free tier implied by 'Benchmark for free')
Bencher Cloud has occasional breaking changes, so exact CLI versions are recommended only for self-hosted use
Some directories named 'plus' fall under a separate Bencher Plus License, not Apache-2.0/MIT
